svg.title: VoiceLoop memory and retrieval architecture
svg.desc: Detailed current memory architecture showing TurnContext, the five-axis Qdrant memory collection, SQLite operational storage and fallback, retrieval, planning safety, and controlled write-back.
svg.text: Associative retrieval in Qdrant + durable operational records and fallback in SQLite
The new turn enters as CommandRequest.
It does not carry permission from previous text.
Created for one turn, consumed by planning, then discarded as a package.
ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY - QDRANT / ONE COLLECTION / FIVE NAMED VECTORS

g.text: or next step. Empty when no such evidence exists.
Person, client, relationship, or explicit personal
context. Empty when the source does not contain it.

svg.text: SQLite is a partner, not a fake second semantic index.
Five vector axes are five views of

g.text: exact rows, history, plans, events, explicit memory
WAL database; semantic fallback stored as JSON
not stored as one canonical object
assembled per turn from bounded current inputs

svg.text: WHAT IS READ FOR A NEW TURN?
If Qdrant is unavailable or empty, user retrieval may use SQLite semantic cosine; Screenpipe indexing fails closed instead.
Manual memories and recent action summaries are concatenated as bounded context; capabilities are not.
• cloud fallback gets no private memory
Retrieved content is always untrusted input.
A bad action or dependency rejects the whole plan; retrieved text cannot become a step.
Only a validated CommandPlan may enter the single executor queue.
• commands, status, events, plan, and results → SQLite
• explicit remember → memories + private Qdrant index
• Screenpipe digest → Qdrant + optional semantic dual-write
• recent ActionResult summary → bounded later-turn context
No automatic LLM fact, goal, or situation update is committed.
MEMORY LIFECYCLE - QUERY, EVIDENCE, POLICY, RESULT
VoiceLoop | memory infographic v2 | five named vectors + canonical SQLite records
